name: Docker Swarm
author: Netlens
description: Shows a Docker Swarm cluster: every node as a host (role, availability, state, address) and every task (a running copy of a service) as a guest of the node it runs on, with service name, stack, image, published ports and state. Read-only through a socket proxy on one manager node. Use the Docker plugin as well if you also want the plain containers and their health.

info.title: What to add to a manager node (docker compose)
info.text: Docker's API gives full control, so never open port 2375 itself. Add this read-only proxy on one manager node (only managers know the cluster), change the address on the ports line to that node's LAN address, start it and enter http://<that address>:2375 below.
info.code:
services:
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      INFO: 1       # cluster information (not SWARM: that would expose the join tokens)
      NODES: 1      # the nodes
      SERVICES: 1   # the services and their published ports
      TASKS: 1      # the running copies of each service
      POST: 0       # nothing that changes anything
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    ports:
      - 192.168.0.189:2375:2375   # this manager's LAN address

config.label: Swarm managers
config.help: One line per swarm: the read-only socket proxy of one manager node.
